issues.legal_issue: Abolition of an intermediary land grant does not by itself end an existing landlord–tenant relationship or defeat a tenant’s statutory right to purchase the land.
material_facts: The land was held by its owner as an inam for the performance of services, and the tenants possessed part of it under leases created before the abolition and regrant.
The tenants were declared purchasers under the tenancy legislation, and the tribunal fixed the purchase price.
The owner argued that abolition of the inam ended the tenancies and therefore removed the tenants’ purchase rights.
issues.conclusion: The tenancies continued after abolition, and the tenants remained entitled to purchase under the tenancy legislation; the tribunal could proceed to fix the purchase price.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 4–9 of the Bombay Merged Territories Miscellaneous Alienations Abolition Act, 1955 abolished alienations and provided for occupancy rights but did not extinguish the relationship between an ex-inamdar and existing tenants. Section 28 preserved the application of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948 and the mutual rights and obligations of landlords and tenants except where inconsistent with an express provision of the abolition legislation. Section 32 of the Tenancy Act was not inconsistent with that legislation. The abolition legislation aimed to eliminate intermediaries, not evict tenants. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: statutory_tenant_purchase_proceeding and land_was_held_under_an_abolished_intermediary_grant and tenant_held_under_a_preexisting_lease and abolition_law_preserves_tenancy_rights

predicates.statutory_tenant_purchase_proceeding: A tribunal is considering a tenant’s claim to purchase land under a statutory tenant-purchase scheme.
predicates.land_was_held_under_an_abolished_interme: The landowner held the land under an intermediary grant that was later abolished.
predicates.tenant_held_under_a_preexisting_lease: The tenant held the land under a lease that existed before the grant was abolished.
predicates.abolition_law_preserves_tenancy_rights: The law abolishing the intermediary grant preserves tenancy rights except where they conflict with its express provisions.

issues.definition: When a tenant-purchase proceeding concerns land held under an abolished intermediary grant, the tenant held it under a preexisting lease, and the abolition law preserves tenancy rights, the tenant remains eligible to purchase.

issues.legal_issue: A notice requirement that applies only to tenancies created after the statutory purchase day does not apply to a tenancy that existed before that day merely because the land was later regranted to the owner.
material_facts: The tenants’ leases existed before the statutory purchase day and before occupancy rights were regranted to the owner after abolition of the inam.

The owner argued that abolition and regrant created a new landlord–tenant relationship and that the tenants had lost their purchase right by failing to give the notice required for later-created tenancies.
issues.conclusion: The tenants’ relationship with the owner did not end and restart upon abolition and regrant; the notice requirement for tenancies created after the statutory purchase day did not apply.
issues.legal_principle: Section 32-O of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948 applies only to tenancies created after the tillers’ day. Because the existing landlord–tenant relationship did not end upon abolition and regrant, no new tenancy arose that would attract that section. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.statutory_tenant_purchase_proceeding: A tribunal is considering a tenant’s claim to purchase land under a statutory tenant-purchase scheme.
predicates.tenancy_existed_before_statutory_purchas: The tenant’s tenancy began before the day on which the statutory purchase scheme took effect.
predicates.abolition_and_regrant_did_not_create_a_n: The intermediary grant was abolished and occupancy rights were regranted, but the tenant’s existing tenancy continued rather than being replaced by a new tenancy.

issues.definition: If a tenant-purchase proceeding concerns a tenancy that began before the statutory purchase day and abolition and regrant did not create a new tenancy, the notice requirement for later-created tenancies does not apply.

issues.legal_issue: A restriction on transfer attached to a regrant does not defeat a tenant’s statutory purchase right when the tenant’s lease was created before the regrant.
material_facts: The tenants held the land under leases created before occupancy rights were regranted to the owner after abolition of the inam.
The court considered the effect of a possible condition that the regranted land was not transferable.
issues.conclusion: Even if the regrant carried a nontransferability condition, that condition could not affect the tenants’ statutory right to purchase the land.
issues.legal_principle: Section 32G(6) of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948 provides that a nontransferability condition attached to a regrant under a land-tenure abolition law listed in Schedule III does not affect the purchase right of a person holding the land under a lease created before regrant. The Bombay Merged Territories Miscellaneous Alienations Abolition Act, 1955 was listed in that schedule. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.statutory_tenant_purchase_proceeding: A tribunal is considering a tenant’s claim to purchase land under a statutory tenant-purchase scheme.
predicates.land_was_regranted_with_a_nontransferabi: The land was regranted to its holder subject to a condition that it could not be transferred.
predicates.tenant_held_under_a_lease_created_before: The tenant held the land under a lease created before the land was regranted to its holder.

issues.definition: If a statutory tenant-purchase proceeding concerns land regranted subject to a nontransferability condition and the tenant’s lease predates the regrant, that condition does not bar the tenant’s purchase.
